pr_title: autoid_service,owner: change autoid service's etcd lease to 10s
pr_body:

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #46454

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

Change the lease value from 60s to 10s
When autoid service panic unexpectedly, it wait lease timeout to elect a new leader to recover the service.
60s is a bit too long.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [X] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)

1. start a tiup cluster 
```
tiup playground  --tiflash 0
```

2. start a new tidb at 4001
```
./bin/tidb-server -store=tikv -path=127.0.0.1:2379 --status=10081 -P 4001
```

3. close the old tidb, so the autoid service will be fallover to the new tidb 4001
```
kill  1469782
```

4. restart the old tidb at 4000
```
./bin/tidb-server -P 4000 --store=tikv --host=127.0.0.1 --status=10080 --path=127.0.0.1:2379
```

5. run sysbench test
```
sysbench --config-file=config oltp_insert --tables=4 --auto_inc=on --mysql_storage_engine='innodb */ AUTO_ID_CACHE 1 /*' prepare 
sysbench --config-file=config oltp_insert --tables=4 --auto_inc=on --mysql_storage_engine='innodb */ AUTO_ID_CACHE 1 /*' run 
```

6. when the test is running, force kill tidb 4001, so the autoid service leader killed, see how long it takes to recover

```
kill -9 1470126
```

I devised a test method for this scenario, which proved to be as expected. ## Expected effect - When the autoid owner job crashes, the recovery time of OLTP (insert) is optimized from around 60s to 10s - DDL owner job crash, DDL recovery time is not affected (60s or so) ## Verification method - Modify sysbench, use AUTO_CACHE_ID = 1 option when creating tables - Verify OLTP (insert) scenarios with sysbench oltp_insert - Use the shell to send one ddl statement per second to verify the ddl job scenario - Use v7.1.1 and nightly(7.4-nightly) respectively, start multiple tidb processes with tiup playground, use `kill -9` to kill the tidb process where the owner job is located to confirm the recovery time. ## Verification results ✅ as expected   | v7.1.1 (current status) | v7.4.0-alpha-nightly-20230905 | results -- | -- | -- | -- DDL recovery time | 82s | 85s | ✅ unchanged OLTP (insert) recovery time | 52s | 10s | ✅ been sped up ## Details * OLTP (insert) recovery time -- before * OLTP (insert) recovery time -- after * DDL recovery time -- before * DDL recovery time -- after

issue_context.title: When autoid service panic unexpected, the recovering time is a bit too long
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

When autoid service leader panic, the follower need to wait the lease timeout to take over the leader's role.
The lease is 60s, which is a bit too long...

For DDL service, it's also 60s, and it's the default value https://pkg.go.dev/go.etcd.io/etcd/clientv3/concurrency#WithTTL
DDL is offline service, so 60s is tolerable.
But autoid allocating is online service, the custome may not expect it take so long to recover.

review_comments: We can add some commnet here. ```10``` means that autoid service's etcd lease is 10s.
